The kubelet and the propagation remove both replicas 12 s–26.079 s after each fault, thus the Service is empty in each fault. On the empty Service, each request waits for its connect, and it fails at the timeout of 2 s. Thus the slow failures go on until the heal. A request that waits for its connect succeeds when an endpoint comes back. Thus the last failure starts up to 2 s before the heal, and up to 11.199 s after it. Each recovery ends before the next fault. One success resets the readiness debounce, the kubelet probe and the retry window of the client of Redis. Thus each fault is the same as the first one. Each client sends a request each 20 ms, thus approximately 3567–5808 requests fail in each fault, and 10701–17424 in the run
